scope: Bounded review of 14 supplied sources; no claim of exhaustive or current-best literature coverage.

records.correction: Arbitrary-order positive-edge insertions; one word has O(log n) bits. Polynomial postprocessing.
Insertion-only positive edges. Source states space without an explicit bit/word convention; do not equate it with a precise bit bound. The ε exponent remains symbolic.
The old display ε=1/4 was outside the strict theorem range. Figure uses ε=1/8. Remark 3.17 discusses a vanishing failure contribution and handles OPT=0 with high probability.
Unlike the LOCAL implementation, streaming stores a global random permutation. No independent-finite-rank correction is added. Positive-edge insertion stream may be revisited.
At fixed δ this is polylogarithmic in n, but accuracy dependence is exponential. The cost axis suppresses logarithms only after fixing δ.
The approximation constant remains O(1); it is never placed at a made-up numerical factor.
Already needs this memory to test OPT=0. Plot fixes p=1; bound also gives Ω(n) for constant passes. This is a value bound, not a partition frontier.
Formal theorem is quantitative; old vague polylog-space wording replaced. C is a fixed theorem constant, not arbitrary additive coefficient.
At c=1.19 the additive coefficient must be below 0.01. Display uses η=0.005; arbitrary O(n) additive error is not justified.
Shown space exponent 7/8 follows exactly from α=1/2. This is not edge arrival and cannot be merged into that frontier.
Same node-access model as the upper theorem, different additive-error contract. Theorem 3.1 additionally requires Ω(n) bits in one pass for (c,d), 0<d≤n/3.
The numerical approximation constant stays symbolic. The original exact theorem streams labeled edges; variants may add polylogarithmic memory.
Full theorem and probability were unavailable in bounded review. This record stays outside the theorem plot.
0<ε<1; additive error is essential. Storage counts sampled incident edges/vertex IDs. Query lower bounds are not streaming-space lower bounds.
Source is a query theorem, not an explicit streaming theorem. One positive-edge pass resolves the preselected pairs; absent pairs are negative. O(Q) alone requires Q≥n.
α_best is the applicable offline polynomial-time approximation factor, retained symbolically; no numerical current-best factor is assigned.
Lemma 5.4 gives Õ(n/ε²) bits for fixed sketch accuracy. The polynomial-space recovery is a distinct resource contract.

records.theorem: KDD metadata/abstract; Ahn et al. 2021 Introduction §1
records.correction: Original full theorem unavailable in bounded review. The pass bound is corroborated by a subsequent primary paper; no numerical pass coordinate assigned.

Theorem wording says high-probability 3-approximation, but proof simulates randomized Pivot and proves memory success. Figure does not promote this to a high-probability factor. Proof stores O(n log n) edges; use Õ(n) rather than silently equating edges and bits.
Choose k=O(1/ε) for an unrestricted number of clusters; this is maximization, not MinDisagree.
Keep the maximization fraction in its original direction; no invented high-probability qualifier.
The ε^{−3} time factor was missing in the original record. This model is separate from complete ±1 instances.
The lower theorem is explicitly a zero-cost decision bound; it does not cover the complete unit-weight partition setting.
Two adversarial-order edge passes. Keep ε fixed in the displayed Õ expression; source does not supply polynomial-time exact coreset optimization.

materialFindings: AKP25 Corollaries 1.3/1.4 bound streaming synopsis memory only; Remark 1.5 permits polynomial postprocessing space. Keep separate from a total-space frontier.
Cambus et al. require 0<ε<1/4; original ε=1/4 chart point removed. ε=1/8 is the default.
ASW23 supplement Theorem 4: Ω(n^ε) bits for a fixed-theorem-constant C times n^(2−ε) purely additive error, success≥0.99.
ASW23 supplement Theorem 5: c∈[1,6/5), 0<η<6/5−c. At c=1.19, η must be below 0.01; arbitrary O(n) error is too broad.
ASW23 expected value theorem retains lower-side success qualification: estimate≥OPT with high probability, expected upper value≤3OPT+δn².
Node upper theorem uses retained-item comparisons, O(1) passes, and α∈[0,1). It is not comparable to edge streams without changing access.
García-Soriano et al. Theorem 3.4 is a nonadaptive query theorem. One-pass streaming is a derived implementation with O(n+Q) words, not a directly stated source theorem.
Bhaskara et al. dense coreset approximates MaxAgree objective, not a full n-label partition in sublinear memory.
AW22 Theorem 7 uses O(n log n) machine words; positive-only and turnstile variants may add polylogarithmic factors.
Ahn Theorem 12 high-probability wording conflicts with the inspected expected-Pivot reasoning; conservatively retained as qualified related evidence.
SODA 2023 full text and KDD 2014 original theorem were unavailable in bounded review; records explicitly marked as abstract or corroborated citations.
unitPolicy: Words and bits remain in each formula. Only the value chart suppresses logarithms to show the exponent of n; fixed accuracy parameters are declared. No unknown ε exponent or numerical α_best is invented.
lowerBoundPolicy: Only verified value and weighted zero-cost decision lower bounds are red. No universal partition barrier or query-to-space lower-bound conversion is drawn.

representation.partition: Exact approximation/pass coordinates for fixed ε and integer-r instances; each theorem retains its own memory formula.
representation.value: Shared exponent-of-n memory axis with distinct error/access rows. Expected, high-probability, purely multiplicative, purely additive, mixed error, and node arrival remain explicit.
representation.weighted: Related evidence cards, with green algorithm/red lower-bound styling.
representation.synopsis: Related resource contract, clearly labeled larger polynomial recovery memory.
